column1: # hal_exceptions.tsv - per-line HAL exceptions under D-40 (zero unjustified waivers), 2026-11-20.
# Read by tools/hal_zero.py after flow/2_static/hal_rules.tsv. One row per RTL line and rule:
# `text` is the signal or port name from HAL's message, so a row covers that line in every
# instance of its module and nothing else. A row that matches no finding fails the gate.
# Each class is a structure the chip must have:

# class CLOCK_GEN: clk_div makes aon/hclk/pclk from refclk: toggle flops, a glitch-free select moved on the falling edge, pclk as a blocking toggle (SIM-1); GARUDA-CLKRST-SPEC-001 5.1, 7.1, 7.6; timed by the SDC generated clocks

# class ICG: the core clock gate (CORE [N-7.27]): an enable latch open while hclk is low and an AND; a library ICG cell replaces it at synthesis (flow/pd/asap7/core_clk_gate_icg.sv); the one latch of the chip
# class JTAG_STD: IEEE 1149.1 TAP: TDO and its enable change on the falling edge of TCK, TCK is a second master clock crossing to hclk through dmi_cdc (CDC run)

# class PAD_RING: the chip top's bidirectional pins (I2C open drain, GPIO, SPI slave MISO, JTAG TDO): tri-state drivers at the pins, replaced by pad cells (rtl/tech, plan 3.8); checked by chip_pads_sva

# class RESET_GEN: reset_ctrl and core_rst_sync generate every reset: synchroniser first stages take a constant 1, request flops drive asynchronous resets (active high where the request is), the cause register samples the request (CLKRST spec 7.2 to 7.6, D-14, D-36); RDC by JasperGold

# class RESET_VALUE: a register whose reset value has both 1 and 0 bits (NOP 0x13, SIZE word, IDCODE, boot PC, stretch count): its bits are async-set and async-cleared, which HAL calls drivers of different types
# class RESET_HANDSHAKE: a reset deassertion sampled as data to release logic in order ([N-9.2], [N-9.3]: the bridge holds HREADYOUT low until PRESETn is released; the watchdog's reset-cause flag)
# class SOFT_RESET: I2C CTRL.RST: a register-driven reset of the vendored byte controller that also clears the wrapper's command bits (GARUDA-I2C-SPEC soft reset)

# class MEMORY_ARRAY: storage with no reset by design: register file (CORE 4), SRAM behavioural model and its read register, the SPI slave RX FIFO entries; contents are undefined until written; the SRAM model's IS_ROM and INIT_FILE are fixed per instance until the SRAM macros (stated open item, G3 3.10)

# class APB_REG_MAP: register map: write-data bits beyond a register's fields are not stored and reserved bits read 0 (each block's register table); PREADY is constant 1 because no peripheral inserts wait states (AHB2APB spec 7.5)
# class PROTOCOL_CONST: AHB outputs that are constant for a master that never does that kind of transfer (instruction port: read, word, no write data; SBA and LSU fixed size bits)

# class DECODE_FIELD: input bits a block does not decode by design: address bits decoded upstream by the AHB decoder, HTRANS[0] (SEQ/NONSEQ) where only HTRANS[1] matters, opcode bits an immediate or DSU decoder does not use, MTVEC mode bits
# class DATAPATH: arithmetic sized on purpose: mul32's 33x33 product (MULH variants), the DSU carry-save shift that drops the top carry by design

# class VENDOR_PORT: an output of vendored IP that GARUDA's wrapper does not use (the IP's own PREADY, constant 1: the shim answers PREADY; the I2C byte controller's direct SCL output, replaced by the wrapper's open-drain enables)

# class COUNTER_WRAP: a counter that wraps by design (FIFO pointers one bit wider than the index, the SPI bit counter 7 to 0) or is cleared at its limit before it can (PWM prescaler at PRESCALE, period counter below PERIOD)
# class CHECKER_USE: a constant read only by the bound properties, which HAL does not compile (soc_map_pkg ID_SOFTWARE, clic_sva)

# class VENDOR_WIDTH: vendored IP (D-40, reviewed 2026-11-20): unequal operand widths, truncated constants and implicit integer conversions; Verilog extends the narrower operand and every case gives the value the IP intends (counters wrap, a count-1 compare with a count of 0 never matches: right for 0); covered by the IP's block tests and the Superlint overflow review (VENDOR_COUNTER)

# class VENDOR_ASSIGN: vendored IP: a process assigns a default then overrides it, or another process reads a variable assigned with blocking assignments; the same in simulation and synthesis (local synthesis: no latch but the ICG); covered by the IP's block tests
# class VENDOR_ONEBIT: vendored IP: bitwise ~ & | in a condition on 1-bit operands (resets, enables, single bits), identical to the logical operator; each line read

# class VENDOR_CASE: vendored IP: a case without default in a clocked block (registers hold, no latch), full_case pragmas on cases that list every value the register can take or carry a default, and a redundant default; each read
# class VENDOR_SPIM_MODE: vendored SPI master state MODE has no exit and is never entered in GARUDA's single-bit configuration (SPIM-2, dispositioned 2026-10-14)

# class VENDOR_PORT: vendored IP outputs the GARUDA configuration does not use (busy and ready flags of the UART's sub-blocks, the IP's own PREADY: the shim answers PREADY, the I2C byte controller's direct SCL output)
# class VENDOR_NORESET: the OpenCores I2C bit controller's dout and dscl_oen: one-cycle delayed copies without reset that follow their source within one pclk (also in the CDC waivers)
# class VENDOR_INDEX: vendored SPI FIFO indexed by pointers that wrap at BUFFER_DEPTH-1 (spi_master_fifo.sv:110-125), so the index never leaves the buffer; HAL cannot see the wrap
# class VENDOR_ELSE: OpenCores I2C byte controller: an else after nested ifs binds to the inner if, which is the intended branch (ST_WRITE: cnt_done)
# class SPEC_PORT: a port kept on the list by the spec's interface contract and read only by the bound properties (bridge pclk_phase_i, AHB2APB spec)
